spans.text: Over a long enough period, the average number of items in a system equals their arrival rate times the average time each spends inside.

meaning.text: Items in the system = arrival rate × time in the system.

spans.text: It holds whatever the arrival pattern, variability or order of service,
but only while items leave as fast as they arrive; a backlog that grows every week breaks it.
expected time in the system ≈ work in progress ÷ throughput
— thirty items in progress at ten finished a week means about three weeks for a new item.
Starting more work to speed up delivery: at the same throughput, more work in progress lengthens waits in exactly the same proportion.
